doc.title: Charles Tolliver interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 6, 2021 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Founding Strata-East Records and its upcoming celebration
summary: Tolliver and Stanley Cowell started the label in 1971 to fill a vacuum for new artists, run mom-and-pop style; he lacks all the original records.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Well thanks for sharing your opinions about that. I was very happy to learn from you on the phone about the upcoming celebration of Strata-East Records. And could you tell me a little bit about that?

Well things got up and running in 1971, you know, brought about by dearly departed Stanley Cowell and myself. And it was probably at the right moment that something like that could be done. Because there was a vacuum that had been created for bringing on new guys into recording and getting them out there like it was with the Blue Notes and Prestiges and all the other smaller independent labels who were issuing product. And it sort of was a labor of love so to speak, and just little by little you know it started to catch on with some musicians and we started issuing product and mom’d and pop’d it along.

Basically mom’d and pop’d it along ‘til now you know. It wasn’t going for the big home run you know, just getting a product out there where the fans would get a hold of it. It was a lot easier in the first ten years because you had record stores and as long as you kept the records in the bins somehow, most of the fans of the music they’d pick up on it.
Do you still have original copies of the 60 plus records that Strata-East issued?
I wish I had. I mean but there are people who do have them.

And they go for a very hefty — you know — in order, if you want to get one. I mean I have a number of them but I don’t think I have all the ones that came through, the first, because most of them came through in the first ten years you know.
I think you and I ought to start a, oh I don’t know, a GoFundMe so we can get you all your original Strata-East records back.
Oh boy. Well yeah, you’d get some hefty funding there maybe.
